title: Adaptive stochastic optimization: a framework for analyzing stochastic optimization algorithms
contribution: Magazine overview arguing for adaptive stochastic optimization methods over nonadaptive, tuned SG methods for ML/SP (abstract).
problem_entry: Criticises SG-based methods as nonadaptive, with prescribed parameters tuned per application (abstract).
key_idea: Summarizes research on adaptive stochastic methods and motivates future work; framework details not in abstract (abstract).
positioning: Written for ML and signal-processing readers, framing SG tuning as the problem (abstract).
limits_future: Claims potential, not demonstrated, computational savings; motivates future work (abstract).

method_links.note: Counts per-application tuning as a cost of the SG baseline (weak link).

quotes.text: Contemporary approaches based on the stochastic gradient (SG) method are nonadaptive in the sense that their implementation employs prescribed parameter values that need to be tuned for each application.

title: A decomposition algorithm with fast identification of critical contingencies for large-scale security-constrained AC-OPF
contribution: Decomposition algorithm of Team GO-SNIP (second place, ARPA-E GO Competition Challenge 1) with contingency ranking and handling of complementarity and degeneracy (abstract).
problem_entry: Application-driven: ARPA-E Grid Optimization Competition Challenge 1, 2018-2019 (abstract).
key_idea: Master problem approximating the security-constrained problem, populated by contingency ranking and evaluation; strategies for complementarity constraints and degeneracies (abstract).
experiments: Extensive experiments illustrating the effectiveness of each technique separately (abstract).
limits_future: Algorithm plus software implementation details; competition result (abstract).

method_links.note: Per-technique evaluation, consistent with ablating each component.

coauthors: DK Molzahn, S Tu, A Wächter, E Wei, E Wong

quotes.text: Software implementation details are described, and the results of an extensive set of numerical experiments are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of each of the used techniques.

title: A stochastic inexact sequential quadratic optimization algorithm for nonlinear equality-constrained optimization
contribution: Stochastic SQP for equality constraints that uses only stochastic objective gradients and inexact subproblem solutions, with convergence results and experiments (abstract).
problem_entry: Equality-constrained problems with exact constraints but stochastic objective information, at a scale where subproblem matrices cannot be formed or factorized (abstract).
key_idea: Inexactness conditions on subproblem solutions that account for stochastic gradient estimates; no objective function values used (abstract).
assumptions: Exact constraint values and derivatives; stochastic objective gradients under a relatively weak set of assumptions (abstract).
experiments: Vastly outperforms a stochastic subgradient method; can outperform an SQP method with highly accurate subproblem solutions (abstract).
limits_future: Algorithm, convergence results and experiments; limits not stated in the abstract.

method_links.note: Subproblem termination conditions derived from the needs of the outer stochastic method.
Rival differs only in subproblem accuracy (highly accurate solves each iteration).

transferable: When making an inner solve inexact, benchmark against the same outer method with highly accurate inner solves to isolate the effect of inexactness (abstract).

quotes.text: Conditions are imposed on the inexact subproblem solutions that account for the fact that only stochastic objective gradient estimates are employed.

title: Fair machine learning through constrained stochastic optimization and an ε-constraint method
contribution: Fair supervised learning posed as loss minimization under a bound on unfairness, swept by an epsilon-constraint method and solved by a scalable stochastic constrained algorithm (abstract).
problem_entry: Fair supervised learning with a prescribed bound on an unfairness measure such as disparate impact (abstract).
key_idea: Embed the constrained problem in an epsilon-constraint multiobjective method to trace the loss-unfairness Pareto front; scalable stochastic solver (abstract).
limits_future: Hedged claim: evidence the strategy can be effective for large-scale fair learning (abstract).

method_links.note: Criterion imposed as a hard constraint with prescribed bound instead of a penalty weight; fits the post-2024 turn away from penalties.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: constraint, not regularizer, for ML desiderata
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Unfairness bounded as a constraint and swept by epsilon rather than penalized.

transferable: Make a secondary training criterion a constraint and sweep its bound (epsilon-constraint) to draw a Pareto front instead of reporting a few penalty weights (abstract).

quotes.text: It involves formulating an optimization problem to minimize loss subject to a prescribed bound on a measure of unfairness (e.g., disparate impact).

title: A Bilevel Optimization Approach for Computing Synthetic Data to Mitigate Unfairness in Collaborative Machine Learning

experiments: Empirical results show reduced unfairness; data sets and baselines not read (abstract).
positioning: Avoids fairness-specific aggregation at the server (abstract).
